extracted.intended_audience: typographers, typesetters, book designers, and printers
extracted.subtask_description: A printed type specimen sheet showing the same sample text and assorted glyphs set in multiple typefaces, point sizes, and spacing (solid vs leaded) to evaluate legibility, appearance, and character repertoire. Used by designers/printers to compare faces and sizes for book typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface family labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings such as "OLD STYLE", "MONOTYPE", "UNOTYPE" and similar identify the typeface or family used for each specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens are grouped and clearly labeled by face name so readers can compare the same sample across different type families; include the face name prominently on the specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-size specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen is identified by a point-size caption such as "FIVE POINT NO. EIGHTY-THREE", "SIX POINT NO. EIGHT", "SEVEN POINT NO. EIGHT", etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label every sample with its point size (and specimen number when used) so designers can assess scale and choose appropriate sizes for setting text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid vs leaded demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections marked "[Solid]" and "[Leaded]" show the same text with different vertical spacing (no extra leading vs with leading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show both solid and leaded settings of the same text to evaluate legibility and aesthetic effect at each point size; explicitly mark which is which.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative body-text sample
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous prose passage (e.g., the Polybius/ Alexander passage beginning "When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...") is used repeatedly to demonstrate how the face performs in typical running copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a long, varied prose sample to reveal word spacing, hyphenation, line breaks, rhythm, and overall readability across sizes and faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-set and glyph repertoire display
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences like "AEIOU", accented/diacritic variants, ligature-like groupings, and assorted letter clusters are printed to show available glyph forms (e.g., "AEIOU A^lOtJ AfetOtJ AMOtJ ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include uppercase/lowercase, diacritics, ligatures, and unusual letter combinations so the specimen demonstrates the face's full glyph coverage and special characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals and punctuation rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Strings such as "1234567890" and repeated numeral fragments appear throughout specimens to display numerals and their spacing in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print contiguous numeral sequences and punctuation within samples so users can judge figure weight, alignment, and legibility at each size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uppercase/display and emphasis examples
rubrics_metrics.description: All-caps lines and emphasized passages (e.g., "A WORLD-EMPIRE, INCLUDING THE LANDS AND NATIONS ABOUT THE MEDITERRANEAN SEA") illustrate how the face behaves in display use and for emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show examples of capitals, small caps or emphasized text so designers can assess display use, hierarchy, and the impact of uppercase settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-size comparison on the same sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The same or similar sample text is repeated across many point sizes (from very small six-point specimens up through larger sizes) on one sheet for side-by-side visual comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a range of sizes together so readers can compare readability, color, and texture of type across sizes before selecting a specific size for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen labelling and typographic notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen includes explicit labels (face, point size, solid/leaded) and occasionally typographic annotations such as bracketed notes (e.g., "[Solid]", "[Leaded]").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure specimens are annotated with clear, consistent labels and any notes about composition so users understand the conditions under which the sample was set.
